newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk cb fund takes over Turkbank's administration.
newsitem.headline: Turk cb fund takes over Turkbank's administration.

text.p: The Turkish central bank said on Friday its Savings and Deposits Insurance Fund had taken over the administration of the troubled Turk Ticaret Bankasi A.S. (Turkbank) this week.
It said Turkbank, which was under the Treasury's surveillance, will continue its operations under the 100 percent guarantee of the central bank fund.
It was planned that the bank be prepared for privatisation by a two-year period of restructuring, the central bank said in a statement.

"It is intended that the bank, which will continue its operations under the control of the Savings and Deposits Insurance Fund, will be restructured in the coming two years and sold by the Privatisation Administration," it said.
Turkbank is 85.2 percent owned by the bank's own pension fund and foundations, while the Treasury owns a further 13.5 percent.
The bank, which employs 4,929 people at its 274 branches in Turkey, was established in 1913.
Last year, the bank achieved a net profit of 234 billion trillion lira, down sharply from 1.6 trillion in 1995.
Turkbank has a paid-up capital of three trillion lira and assets of 210.4 trillion lira -- 2.3 percent of the total Turkish banking sector.
Its capital adequacy ratio fell to 4.9 perent last year from 7.5 percent in 1995, according to a report of the Turkish Banks' Association.
